summary: The group is mostly in good shape for line operations (line-chunk, line-segmentize, line-smooth, offset-curve, line-simplification, linear-referencing) whose headline value is already per-frame; most of those only need a distance-based binding instead of x. The weakest pictures are coverage-validity (every edge orange at defaults), coverage-simplification (rectilinear Chicago tracts barely simplify), segment-ring-assembly (the single output ring lies on the input), constrained-delaunay-triangulation (identical to polygon-triangulation, and at runtime it scrubs Data: irregularity) and shape-generator (small rings in one corner). Ten runs scrub a Data: parameter at runtime and seven scrub by full rebuild (concave hulls, dorling, isovists, visibility graph, offset expansion). The urban recipes (isovists, tessellation, adjacency, visibility graph, street profiles) are the most explanatory and become excellent with place/drag/probe on the Overtoom footprints. Shared fixes: a CPU nearest-line/vertex/projection helper in shared/lines.ts serves eleven reach bindings; separate shiftX/shiftY in polygon-overlay and line-clip; per-building offsets in shared/urban.ts; min-angle coloring and vertex drag in shared/triangulation.ts; irregular boundaries and per-tract gaps in shared/tract-coverage.ts.

sharedChanges.change: Add CPU helpers: nearest line/segment to a point with projection, measure along the line and signed perpendicular distance, plus nearest vertex; pointer bindings for reach, place and level all need them.
Let getBuildings translate or recede one building by index, and add a point-in-footprint lookup, so drag/probe can move a single footprint per frame.
Add a per-vertex offset to getSet for vertex drag, color triangles by minimum angle, and pre-build snapped maximumFlips variants so CDT and ear clipping look different.
Offer a coverage with irregular shared boundaries and a per-edge defect generator (sliver gap, overlap, mismatched vertex) instead of rectilinear tracts and a uniform shrink.
Split the single shift into shiftX/shiftY (createBlobSet already accepts both) for a 2D drag; the same edit applies to line-clip-by-polygon.ts.
Add a small highlight pass (write a flag per element when its id equals a per-frame uniform) so probe can brighten a chain, ring, district, terrace or node's edges without a rebuild.

frameworkNeeds: a defineOperationRun pointer hook (pointer in drawing-world coordinates, hover and leave) that writes values or buffers through update, instead of the generic x scrub
cursor glyph overlay: ring of a given radius, disc, corridor band along a polyline, perpendicular tick, crosshair, playhead line
readout text built by the run (value, unit and an output count read from a status buffer)
highlight-by-id on segments, lines, polygons and chart bars layers (per-frame uniform id)
snapped and debounced rebuild for compile-time props, or a cache of pre-built variants keyed by value
small async readback of status counts (pieces, flagged edges, kept vertices) for readouts

issues.detail: The first line from createLineSet(2, 16) is a straight horizontal stroke along the top edge, so half the input says little about joins and merging.
issues.fix: Use two bending river lines (createRiverBend like offset-curve) that pass close to each other so the merged surface visibly fuses.

proposal.glyph: dashed perpendicular from the nearest input point to the cursor, its length equal to the buffer width

issues.detail: maximumCircumradius is a compile-time constant (MAXIMUM_CIRCUMRADIUS), so every scrub step recompiles.

issues.detail: At the default maximumFlips 40 the picture is indistinguishable from polygon-triangulation (same blobs, seed and colors).
issues.fix: Color each triangle by its minimum angle (slivers warm, well-shaped cool) so the flips are visible, and default to a low flip cap.

issues.detail: The census says maximumFlips, but at runtime maximumFlips is in rebuildOn and the helper has update, so the card scrubs 'Data: irregularity'.
issues.fix: Bind the pointer to maximumFlips (below) or mark it cardScrub.

issues.detail: default maximumFlips = max (40) so the reader never sees the unflipped slivers.
issues.fix: Default to a small cap (2 to 4).

proposal.binding: x -> maximumFlips as a playhead 1..40, snapped to 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 40
proposal.glyph: thin playhead line with flip count; slivers recolor as they flip
proposal.feasibilityNote: maximumFlips is a WGSL loop bound; pre-build the six variants (6 small polygons) and switch between them.

issues.detail: Chicago tracts are almost rectilinear, so Douglas-Peucker removes few vertices and the simplified rings sit on the originals.
issues.fix: Use a coverage with wiggly shared boundaries (lake shore or river-following tracts, or a Voronoi coverage with jittered edges).

issues.detail: Input (muted, radius 3) and output (radius 1.8) overlap almost exactly at the default tolerance.
issues.fix: Draw dropped vertices as dots and offset the output color strongly; pick a jagged dataset as above.

issues.detail: At defaults (gap 0.012 < gapWidth 0.03) every shared edge is flagged, so the whole picture is orange and nothing is singled out.
issues.fix: Vary the gap per tract (most exactly touching, a few slivers, one overlap) so only some edges flag; default gapWidth between those gaps.

issues.detail: A uniform shrink of every cell is not how invalid coverages occur.
issues.fix: Perturb a few shared edges only (sliver gap, overlap, mismatched vertex) on otherwise valid tracts.
